fact: Nvidia and SpaceX announced a partnership to develop GPUs for SpaceX's planned orbital data centers, and Elon Musk said a space-optimized Vera Rubin NVL72 system had been designed that SpaceX plans to launch into orbit toward the end of 2027 and scale in 2028 (Motley Fool, 2026-09-27).
why: A customer's plan to launch a special variant in late 2027 falls about eleven months after P's January 31, 2027 cutoff and says nothing on whether shipping starts before that date.

fact: AWS has a stated plan to deploy NVIDIA Rubin GPUs by the end of calendar 2027 (conveyed only in Q's focus line and previous conclusion, with no statement id, date or quoted passage).
why: As conveyed, the plan is bounded only by December 31, 2027, so it cannot tell shipping before January 31, 2027 from shipping after it.

fact: NVIDIA reported purchase orders for Vera Rubin from every major hyperscaler, AI cloud provider and system OEM (via MarketBeat, 2026-09-25).
why: Orders from every large customer corroborate that the reported August production shipments are commercial deliveries, which an analyst would weigh as support for shipping having begun.

fact: NVIDIA management expects Vera Rubin to bring in about 20% of data-center revenue in fiscal Q3 2027 (via trefis.com, 2026-09-27 and 2026-09-28).
why: A sizeable revenue share in a quarter that ends more than a year before the deadline implies Rubin is being shipped and billed in volume, which an analyst would weigh as support for Yes.

fact: NVIDIA management expects sales to its largest cloud-company customers to accelerate again in fiscal Q4 2027 as Vera Rubin supply grows (via trefis.com, 2026-09-27).
why: Growing Vera Rubin supply to the largest cloud customers in fiscal Q4 2027 is a statement about delivery timing well inside the deadline, and it speaks to the same kind of customer as the AWS plan Q's reference rests on.

fact: NVIDIA management said on the fiscal Q2 2027 call that inventory rose to $32 billion as the company prepared for the Vera Rubin launch (via trefis.com, 2026-09-28).
why: An inventory build made for the launch is evidence on when the launch happens, which an analyst would weigh as corroboration that shipping starts long before the deadline.

fact: MarketBeat judges that much of Oracle's backlog is back-ended and waiting for the next-generation performance expected from Vera Rubin (2026-09-25).
why: It is an outside view on when one customer's demand lands, not on whether or when NVIDIA begins shipping Rubin GPUs.

fact: NVIDIA expects revenue of $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, for fiscal Q3 2027 (in the Zacks passage quoted under e113, 2026-09-24).
why: Company-wide revenue guidance does not say whether or when Rubin GPUs ship.

answers: Both answers are 1 (Yes) and both rest on the same report that production shipments began in August 2026, which both requests convey, so no listed fact produces a different answer. They differ in the starting reference and in the supporting points: Q starts from Yes on the AWS deployment plan and adds the SpaceX late-2027 plan, both absent from P's request, while P starts from a deadline-based No and supports its Yes with the roughly 20% of data-center revenue expected in fiscal Q3 2027, which Q's request lacks; the listed facts explain those omissions. P's answer also leaves out the MLPerf preview item that Q's answer discusses, but P's request did show that item, so no listed fact explains that omission.
